paragraphs.text: ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד וְאַתָּה֙ לֹ֣א שָׁד֔וּד וּבוֹגֵ֖ד וְלֹא־בָ֣גְדוּ ב֑וֹ כַּהֲתִֽמְךָ֤ שׁוֹדֵד֙ תּוּשַּׁ֔ד כַּנְּלֹתְךָ֥ לִבְגֹּ֖ד יִבְגְּדוּ־בָֽךְ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Woe to you, destroyer, who were not destroyed, and treacherous one, with whom they did not deal treacherously! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; when you have made an end of dealing treacherously, they will deal treacherously with you.
i18n.he: ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד וְאַתָּה֙ לֹ֣א שָׁד֔וּד וּבוֹגֵ֖ד וְלֹא־בָ֣גְדוּ ב֑וֹ כַּהֲתִֽמְךָ֤ שׁוֹדֵד֙ תּוּשַּׁ֔ד כַּנְּלֹתְךָ֥ לִבְגֹּ֖ד יִבְגְּדוּ־בָֽךְ׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*hôy šôḏēḏ … ûḇôḡēḏ*: the woe opens on two participles addressed to the enemy, so the line reads "Woe to you, destroyer … treacherous one" (overlay `hoy-woe-isaiah`: "Woe to …" before a participle). The pair *šdd* "destroy" and *bgd* "deal treacherously" is the paronomasia of 21:2 and 24:16 and takes the same English family (overlay `bgd-shdd-treachery-destroyer-isaiah`). ASV has "destroyest … dealest treacherously", JPS 1917 "spoilest … dealest treacherously", NJPS "ravager … betrayer" (all checked 2026-11-26).

Two forms are uncertain. *kahătimmᵉḵā* is taken from *tmm* "be complete": "when you have finished destroying". *kannᵉlōṯᵉḵā* occurs only here. ASV's "when thou hast made an end" connects it with *klh* "finish" (often by emending to *kᵉḵallōṯᵉḵā*; recalled, not verified), and JPS 1917's "when thou art weary" connects it with *lʾh* "be weary". The line follows ASV, which keeps the two clauses parallel (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`).

In *wᵉlōʾ-ḇāḡᵉḏû bô* the suffix is third person ("with him") inside second-person address. The relative "with whom" keeps the sense without forcing the person. The bgd entry records that NJPS emends the actives of 21:2 to passives by comparison with this verse; here MT is kept (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: יְהוָ֥ה חָנֵּ֖נוּ לְךָ֣ קִוִּ֑ינוּ הֱיֵ֤ה זְרֹעָם֙ לַבְּקָרִ֔ים אַף־יְשׁוּעָתֵ֖נוּ בְּעֵ֥ת צָרָֽה׃

i18n.en: YHWH, be gracious to us; for you we have waited. Be their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
i18n.he: יְהוָ֥ה חָנֵּ֖נוּ לְךָ֣ קִוִּ֑ינוּ הֱיֵ֤ה זְרֹעָם֙ לַבְּקָרִ֔ים אַף־יְשׁוּעָתֵ֖נוּ בְּעֵ֥ת צָרָֽה׃

notes.official: *hĕyēh zᵉrōʿām labbᵉqārîm* "be their arm every morning". MT has a third-person plural suffix, although the rest of the prayer speaks in the first person ("be gracious to us … our salvation"). ASV prints "our arm", which presupposes the emendation *zᵉrōʿēnû*. JPS 1917 and NJPS keep "their arm", and NJPS notes that "Emendation yields 'You have been our help'" (all checked 2026-11-26). The line translates MT and so departs from ASV (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). "Their" can refer to the people for whom the speakers pray; the emendation treats it as a slip for "our". *labbᵉqārîm* is distributive, "every morning" (ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS).

paragraphs.text: מִקּ֣וֹל הָמ֔וֹן נָדְד֖וּ עַמִּ֑ים מֵר֣וֹמְמֻתֶ֔ךָ נָפְצ֖וּ גּוֹיִֽם׃

i18n.en: At the sound of the tumult the peoples have fled; at your lifting up of yourself the nations are scattered.
i18n.he: מִקּ֣וֹל הָמ֔וֹן נָדְד֖וּ עַמִּ֑ים מֵר֣וֹמְמֻתֶ֔ךָ נָפְצ֖וּ גּוֹיִֽם׃

notes.official: *mērômᵉmuṯeḵā* "at your lifting up of yourself" is a noun of *rwm* "be high" found only here (BDB; recalled). ASV and JPS 1917 have "at the lifting up of thyself", NJPS "Before Your majesty". The line keeps ASV's sense, since "majesty" in this book renders *gāʾôn* (overlay `gaon-pride-human-arrogance-isaiah`). *qôl hāmôn* is "the sound of the tumult" (ASV "the noise of the tumult"); NJPS supplies "[Your] roaring".

paragraphs.text: וְאֻסַּ֣ף שְׁלַלְכֶ֔ם אֹ֖סֶף הֶֽחָסִ֑יל כְּמַשַּׁ֥ק גֵּבִ֖ים שׁוֹקֵ֥ק בּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And your spoil shall be gathered as the caterpillar gathers; as locusts leap, so they leap upon it.
i18n.he: וְאֻסַּ֣ף שְׁלַלְכֶ֔ם אֹ֖סֶף הֶֽחָסִ֑יל כְּמַשַּׁ֥ק גֵּבִ֖ים שׁוֹקֵ֥ק בּֽוֹ׃

notes.official:
The verse is obscure in every version. *ʾōsep̄ he-ḥāsîl* is "as the caterpillar gathers" (ASV, JPS 1917). *ḥāsîl* is a locust or a stage of one (BDB; Joel 1:4; recalled), and the line keeps the traditional English insect name. *kᵉmaššaq gēḇîm šôqēq bô* is read with ASV from *šqq* "run to and fro, rush": "as locusts leap, so they leap upon it". ASV supplies "men" as the subject of the singular participle; the line uses an indefinite "they", because the Hebrew has no human noun. NJPS takes *šqq* as a cognate of a verb of gathering ("It was amassed as grasshoppers are amassed") and marks the meaning uncertain (checked).

*wᵉʾussap̄* (waw with a perfect) is future in ASV, present in JPS 1917 ("is gathered") and past in NJPS ("was gathered"). The line follows ASV (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`).

paragraphs.text: נִשְׂגָּ֣ב יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י שֹׁכֵ֖ן מָר֑וֹם מִלֵּ֣א צִיּ֔וֹן מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃

i18n.en: YHWH is exalted, for he dwells on high; he has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
i18n.he: נִשְׂגָּ֣ב יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י שֹׁכֵ֖ן מָר֑וֹם מִלֵּ֣א צִיּ֔וֹן מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃

notes.official: *nisgāḇ YHWH kî šōḵēn mārôm* "YHWH is exalted, for he dwells on high". The verb is *šāḵan* "dwell" (central `shakhan-dwell-divine-presence-verb-cross-corpus`), and v. 16 repeats it of the righteous person, "he shall dwell on high" (*mᵉrômîm yiškōn*), so the chapter sets the two dwellings side by side. *mišpāṭ ûṣᵉḏāqāh* "justice and righteousness" is the fixed pair in the same order as 9:6 (central `tzedakah-u-mishpat-justice-pair`); the line keeps the Hebrew order.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה֙ אֱמוּנַ֣ת עִתֶּ֔יךָ חֹ֥סֶן יְשׁוּעֹ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת וָדָ֑עַת יִרְאַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה הִ֥יא אוֹצָרֽוֹ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And there shall be stability in your times, an abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge; the fear of YHWH is his treasure.
i18n.he: וְהָיָה֙ אֱמוּנַ֣ת עִתֶּ֔יךָ חֹ֥סֶן יְשׁוּעֹ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת וָדָ֑עַת יִרְאַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה הִ֥יא אוֹצָרֽוֹ׃ (ס)

notes.official:
The syntax of the verse is uncertain. ASV reads *ʾĕmûnaṯ ʿittêḵā* as "stability in thy times" and lists "abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge" after it. JPS 1917 makes the phrase the subject ("the stability of thy times shall be a hoard of salvation"), and NJPS has "Faithfulness to Your charge was [her] wealth", marked "Meaning of Heb. uncertain" (all checked 2026-11-26). The line follows ASV. *ʾĕmûnāh* means firmness before it means faithfulness (BDB; recalled), and *ḥōsen* "store, abundance" fits ASV's "abundance" (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`).

In the last clause MT has *ʾôṣārô* "his treasure". ASV prints "thy treasure", in line with the second-person *ʿittêḵā*. JPS 1917 has "His treasure", and NJPS has "her treasure" with the note "Heb. 'his'". The line translates MT and so departs from ASV (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). The antecedent of "his" is not stated. JPS 1917's capital takes it as YHWH, so that the fear of YHWH is what he treasures; it can also be the people addressed, taken as a collective.

paragraphs.text: הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם צָעֲק֖וּ חֻ֑צָה מַלְאֲכֵ֣י שָׁל֔וֹם מַ֖ר יִבְכָּיֽוּן׃

i18n.en: Behold, their valiant ones cry outside; the messengers of peace weep bitterly.
i18n.he: הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם צָעֲק֖וּ חֻ֑צָה מַלְאֲכֵ֣י שָׁל֔וֹם מַ֖ר יִבְכָּיֽוּן׃

notes.official:
*ʾerʾellām* is a crux. ASV and JPS 1917 "their valiant ones" connect it with *ʾărîʾēl* "hero" (2 Sam 23:20; recalled) and read a third-person suffix. NJPS has "The Arielites", noting "So a few manuscripts; cf. 29.1" (checked). That reading makes them the people of Ariel, the cipher-name for Jerusalem at 29:1–7 (overlay `ariel-ob-isaiah-29`, not applied here because MT does not have the name). Others repoint the consonants as *ʾērāʾeh lāhem* "I will appear to them" (recalled, not verified). The line keeps the MT and ASV reading (overlays `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`, `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`).

*malʾăḵê šālôm* is "the messengers of peace". ASV and JPS 1917 have "ambassadors"; the line uses "messengers", the book's English for *malʾāḵ* at 14:32, 18:2, 42:19 and 44:26, so that one noun keeps one English word (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`). NJPS's "Shalom's messengers", which it explains as Jerusalem's (cf. Salem, Ps 76:3), is a reading of the second noun as a name.

paragraphs.text: נָשַׁ֣מּוּ מְסִלּ֔וֹת שָׁבַ֖ת עֹבֵ֣ר אֹ֑רַח הֵפֵ֤ר בְּרִית֙ מָאַ֣ס עָרִ֔ים לֹ֥א חָשַׁ֖ב אֱנֽוֹשׁ׃

i18n.en: The highways lie desolate; the wayfarer has ceased. He has broken the covenant, he has despised the cities, he regards no mortal.
i18n.he: נָשַׁ֣מּוּ מְסִלּ֔וֹת שָׁבַ֖ת עֹבֵ֣ר אֹ֑רַח הֵפֵ֤ר בְּרִית֙ מָאַ֣ס עָרִ֔ים לֹ֥א חָשַׁ֖ב אֱנֽוֹשׁ׃

notes.official:
*nāšammû mᵉsillôṯ šāḇaṯ ʿōḇēr ʾōraḥ* "the highways lie desolate; the wayfarer has ceased". The subject of the next three verbs is not named. ASV supplies "[the enemy]", and the line keeps the bare "He" of the Hebrew.

*māʾas ʿārîm* "he has despised the cities" is MT, with ASV and JPS 1917. NJPS notes that 1QIsaᵃ reads "A pact" (checked as an NJPS note only; the scroll was not consulted), and some modern versions read *ʿēḏîm* "witnesses" (recalled, not verified). MT is kept (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

*lōʾ ḥāšaḇ ʾĕnôš* is "he regards no mortal". *ʾĕnôš* is the generic human noun that the book renders "mortal" at 13:12 and 24:6 (overlay `enosh-mortal-isaiah`). ASV and JPS 1917 have "he regardeth not man", and NJPS "Mortal man despised", with a note that an emendation yields "an obligation" (checked). The draft's "no one" kept the gender-neutral sense but dropped the noun; "mortal" keeps both.

paragraphs.text: אָבַ֤ל אֻמְלְלָה֙ אָ֔רֶץ הֶחְפִּ֥יר לְבָנ֖וֹן קָמַ֑ל הָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרוֹן֙ כָּֽעֲרָבָ֔ה וְנֹעֵ֥ר בָּשָׁ֖ן וְכַרְמֶֽל׃

i18n.en: The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and withers away; Sharon has become like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
i18n.he: אָבַ֤ל אֻמְלְלָה֙ אָ֔רֶץ הֶחְפִּ֥יר לְבָנ֖וֹן קָמַ֑ל הָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרוֹן֙ כָּֽעֲרָבָ֔ה וְנֹעֵ֥ר בָּשָׁ֖ן וְכַרְמֶֽל׃

notes.official:
*ʾāḇal ʾumlᵉlāh ʾāreṣ* "the land mourns and languishes" uses the verb pair of 24:4 and 24:7 ("mourns … languishes"); *ʾereṣ* here is the land of Judah (central `eretz`). *heḥpîr* is "is ashamed" (JPS 1917; ASV "is confounded").

*hāyāh haš-šārôn kāʿărāḇāh* "Sharon has become like a desert". *ʿărāḇāh* can also be the proper name of the rift valley, the Arabah, which would match the three place names around it. The line takes the common noun with ASV, JPS 1917 ("wilderness") and NJPS ("desert"), as the book does at 35:1, 6 and 40:3.

*wᵉnōʿēr bāšān wᵉḵarmel* "and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves". *nōʿēr* is the participle of *nʿr* "shake (off)", the verb of v. 15 ("who shakes his hands"). ASV supplies the object "[their leaves]", which the line prints because English "shake off" needs one; JPS 1917 ("are clean bare") and NJPS ("are stripped bare") read the verb without an object (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`).

paragraphs.text: עַתָּ֥ה אָק֖וּם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה עַתָּה֙ אֵֽרוֹמָ֔ם עַתָּ֖ה אֶנָּשֵֽׂא׃

i18n.en: Now I will arise, says YHWH; now I will lift myself up; now I will be exalted.
i18n.he: עַתָּ֥ה אָק֖וּם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה עַתָּה֙ אֵֽרוֹמָ֔ם עַתָּ֖ה אֶנָּשֵֽׂא׃

paragraphs.text: תַּהֲר֥וּ חֲשַׁ֖שׁ תֵּ֣לְדוּ קַ֑שׁ רוּחֲכֶ֕ם אֵ֖שׁ תֹּאכַלְכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: You shall conceive chaff, you shall bring forth stubble; your breath is a fire that shall devour you.
i18n.he: תַּהֲר֥וּ חֲשַׁ֖שׁ תֵּ֣לְדוּ קַ֑שׁ רוּחֲכֶ֕ם אֵ֖שׁ תֹּאכַלְכֶֽם׃

notes.official: *rûḥăḵem ʾēš tōʾḵalḵem* "your breath is a fire that shall devour you" (ASV, JPS 1917). NJPS has "My breath will devour you like fire", with the note "Heb. 'your'" (checked); some read *kᵉmô ʾēš* "like fire" (recalled, not verified). MT is kept (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`): the enemy's own breath consumes him, as fire consumes the chaff and stubble of the first half of the verse.

paragraphs.text: וְהָי֥וּ עַמִּ֖ים מִשְׂרְפ֣וֹת שִׂ֑יד קוֹצִ֥ים כְּסוּחִ֖ים בָּאֵ֥שׁ יִצַּֽתּוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the peoples shall be as the burnings of lime, as thorns cut down that are burned in the fire.
i18n.he: וְהָי֥וּ עַמִּ֖ים מִשְׂרְפ֣וֹת שִׂ֑יד קוֹצִ֥ים כְּסוּחִ֖ים בָּאֵ֥שׁ יִצַּֽתּוּ׃ (ס)

notes.official: *miśrᵉp̄ôṯ śîḏ* "the burnings of lime": the peoples will be burned as lime is burned (cf. Amos 2:1, bones burned to lime; recalled). NJPS notes that an emendation yields "brambles" (cf. 32:13; checked as an NJPS note). MT is kept (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי וּדְע֥וּ קְרוֹבִ֖ים גְּבֻרָתִֽי׃

i18n.en: Hear, you who are far off, what I have done; and you who are near, acknowledge my might.
i18n.he: שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי וּדְע֥וּ קְרוֹבִ֖ים גְּבֻרָתִֽי׃

paragraphs.text: פָּחֲד֤וּ בְצִיּוֹן֙ חַטָּאִ֔ים אָחֲזָ֥ה רְעָדָ֖ה חֲנֵפִ֑ים מִ֣י ׀ יָג֣וּר לָ֗נוּ אֵ֚שׁ אוֹכֵלָ֔ה מִי־יָג֥וּר לָ֖נוּ מוֹקְדֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling has seized the godless: “Who among us can dwell with the devouring fire? Who among us can dwell with everlasting burnings?”
i18n.he: פָּחֲד֤וּ בְצִיּוֹן֙ חַטָּאִ֔ים אָחֲזָ֥ה רְעָדָ֖ה חֲנֵפִ֑ים מִ֣י ׀ יָג֣וּר לָ֗נוּ אֵ֚שׁ אוֹכֵלָ֔ה מִי־יָג֥וּר לָ֖נוּ מוֹקְדֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃

notes.official:
*mî yāḡûr lānû ʾēš ʾôḵēlāh* "Who among us can dwell with the devouring fire?" *gûr* means "dwell as a guest, sojourn" (BDB; recalled), and it differs from *šāḵan* "dwell" in vv. 5 and 16. The book renders *gûr* "dwell" for a lasting stay (11:6 "the wolf shall dwell with the lamb") and "sojourn" for a stay abroad (16:4; 23:7). Here ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all have "dwell", and the line follows them; the two verbs are recorded in `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`. The question has the form of the entrance liturgies, Ps 15:1 ("who shall sojourn in your tent?", also *gûr*) and Ps 24:3, and vv. 15–16 give the answer.

*môqᵉḏê ʿôlām* "everlasting burnings" (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS "the never-dying blaze"). *môqēḏ* is a hearth or a burning mass (BDB; recalled). The English "burnings" also renders *miśrᵉp̄ôṯ* in v. 12; ASV has the same overlap, and it is kept. *ʾēš ʾôḵēlāh* "devouring fire" recurs at 29:6 and 30:30 (cf. 30:27), and the same phrase describes the glory of YHWH on the mountain at Exod 24:17.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (speculative; reception note, not a translation claim).** The Raëlian canon does not cite Isa 33. *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes Exod 24:17, "the sight of the glory of Yahweh was like devouring fire on the top of the mount", and then explains it (3:33): "There you have the description of the «glory» — in reality the flying craft — of the creators". A reader who follows that reading may hear the same phrase in the fire with which no sinner can dwell. The connection is the Editor's, not the canon's, and the line renders the phrase as the other versions do.

paragraphs.text: הֹלֵ֣ךְ צְדָק֔וֹת וְדֹבֵ֖ר מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים מֹאֵ֞ס בְּבֶ֣צַע מַעֲשַׁקּ֗וֹת נֹעֵ֤ר כַּפָּיו֙ מִתְּמֹ֣ךְ בַּשֹּׁ֔חַד אֹטֵ֤ם אָזְנוֹ֙ מִשְּׁמֹ֣עַ דָּמִ֔ים וְעֹצֵ֥ם עֵינָ֖יו מֵרְא֥וֹת בְּרָֽע׃

i18n.en: He who walks righteously and speaks uprightly, who despises the gain of oppressions, who shakes his hands from taking a bribe, who stops his ears from hearing of blood, and shuts his eyes from looking upon evil —
i18n.he: הֹלֵ֣ךְ צְדָק֔וֹת וְדֹבֵ֖ר מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים מֹאֵ֞ס בְּבֶ֣צַע מַעֲשַׁקּ֗וֹת נֹעֵ֤ר כַּפָּיו֙ מִתְּמֹ֣ךְ בַּשֹּׁ֔חַד אֹטֵ֤ם אָזְנוֹ֙ מִשְּׁמֹ֣עַ דָּמִ֔ים וְעֹצֵ֥ם עֵינָ֖יו מֵרְא֥וֹת בְּרָֽע׃

notes.official: *hōlēḵ ṣᵉḏāqôṯ wᵉḏōḇēr mêšārîm* "he who walks righteously and speaks uprightly" begins the answer to the question of v. 14, in the manner of Ps 15:2–5. *nōʿēr kappāyw* "who shakes his hands" uses the verb of v. 9. *šᵉmōaʿ dāmîm* "hearing of blood" is listening to plans for bloodshed (NJPS "infamy").

paragraphs.text: ה֚וּא מְרוֹמִ֣ים יִשְׁכֹּ֔ן מְצָד֥וֹת סְלָעִ֖ים מִשְׂגַּבּ֑וֹ לַחְמ֣וֹ נִתָּ֔ן מֵימָ֖יו נֶאֱמָנִֽים׃

i18n.en: he shall dwell on high; his place of defense shall be the strongholds of the rocks; his bread shall be given, his water shall be sure.
i18n.he: ה֚וּא מְרוֹמִ֣ים יִשְׁכֹּ֔ן מְצָד֥וֹת סְלָעִ֖ים מִשְׂגַּבּ֑וֹ לַחְמ֣וֹ נִתָּ֔ן מֵימָ֖יו נֶאֱמָנִֽים׃

notes.official: *mᵉrômîm yiškōn* "he shall dwell on high" repeats the verb and the place of v. 5, *šōḵēn mārôm* (central `shakhan-dwell-divine-presence-verb-cross-corpus`). *mᵉṣāḏôṯ sᵉlāʿîm* is "the strongholds of the rocks" (ASV "munitions", an older word for fortifications).

paragraphs.text: מֶ֥לֶךְ בְּיָפְי֖וֹ תֶּחֱזֶ֣ינָה עֵינֶ֑יךָ תִּרְאֶ֖ינָה אֶ֥רֶץ מַרְחַקִּֽים׃

i18n.en: Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty; they shall behold a land that stretches afar.
i18n.he: מֶ֥לֶךְ בְּיָפְי֖וֹ תֶּחֱזֶ֣ינָה עֵינֶ֑יךָ תִּרְאֶ֖ינָה אֶ֥רֶץ מַרְחַקִּֽים׃

notes.official:
*meleḵ bᵉyop̄yô* "the king in his beauty". *yōp̄î* is the ordinary noun "beauty" of the root *yph* "be beautiful" (BDB; recalled). ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all render it "beauty" (checked), and the book prints the same at 3:24 ("branding instead of beauty"). The book also uses "beauty" for *ṣᵉḇî* (overlay `tsevi-beauty-isaiah`). The two nouns never stand in the same Isaiah verse, and no other English word renders *yōp̄î* as plainly, so they share "beauty" and the sharing is recorded (overlay `yofi-beauty-isaiah`).

*meleḵ* has no article. ASV and JPS 1917 have "the king", NJPS "a king", with a note that an emendation yields "perfection of beauty" (cf. Ps 50:2; checked). The line keeps "the king" (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). The verse does not say who the king is. He may be YHWH, called "our king" in v. 22, or the human king of 32:1, and the line leaves the question open. The divine title of 6:5 (overlay `ha-melekh-divine-title-isaiah`) has the article and stands with the divine name, so it is not applied here.

*ʾereṣ marḥaqqîm* "a land that stretches afar" (ASV "a land that reacheth afar"; NJPS "the land round about") is a land of wide distances (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: לִבְּךָ֖ יֶהְגֶּ֣ה אֵימָ֑ה אַיֵּ֤ה סֹפֵר֙ אַיֵּ֣ה שֹׁקֵ֔ל אַיֵּ֖ה סֹפֵ֥ר אֶת־הַמִּגְדָּלִֽים׃

i18n.en: Your heart shall muse on the terror: “Where is the one who counted? Where is the one who weighed? Where is the one who counted the towers?”
i18n.he: לִבְּךָ֖ יֶהְגֶּ֣ה אֵימָ֑ה אַיֵּ֤ה סֹפֵר֙ אַיֵּ֣ה שֹׁקֵ֔ל אַיֵּ֖ה סֹפֵ֥ר אֶת־הַמִּגְדָּלִֽים׃

notes.official:
*libbᵉḵā yehgeh ʾêmāh* "your heart shall muse on the terror": the heart goes back over the past dread. NJPS takes *lēḇ* as "throat" (cf. 59:13) and *hgh* as a sound ("shall murmur in awe"); the line keeps ASV's sense.

The three questions name the officials of the oppressor. *sōp̄ēr* is a participle, "one who counts" (ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS), and the same form is also the title of the scribe or state secretary (BDB; recalled). The line keeps the participle, since the third question has it with an object ("the one who counted the towers"). ASV supplies "[the tribute]" after "weighed"; the Hebrew has no object, and the line adds none (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`). Paul's "Where is the wise? where is the scribe?" (1 Cor 1:20; Greek *poû grammateús*, checked in the corpus) is often connected with this verse and with Isa 19:12 (connection recalled, not verified).

paragraphs.text: אֶת־עַ֥ם נוֹעָ֖ז לֹ֣א תִרְאֶ֑ה עַ֣ם עִמְקֵ֤י שָׂפָה֙ מִשְּׁמ֔וֹעַ נִלְעַ֥ג לָשׁ֖וֹן אֵ֥ין בִּינָֽה׃

i18n.en: You shall not see the fierce people, a people of speech too deep to comprehend, of a stammering tongue that cannot be understood.
i18n.he: אֶת־עַ֥ם נוֹעָ֖ז לֹ֣א תִרְאֶ֑ה עַ֣ם עִמְקֵ֤י שָׂפָה֙ מִשְּׁמ֔וֹעַ נִלְעַ֥ג לָשׁ֖וֹן אֵ֥ין בִּינָֽה׃

notes.official:
*nilʿaḡ lāšôn* is "of a stammering tongue" (JPS 1917 "Of a stammering tongue"; NJPS "So stammering of tongue"; ASV "of a strange tongue"; all checked). The root *lʿg* "stammer, mock" is the root of *laʿăḡê śāp̄āh* "stammering lips" at 28:11, and both verses describe the same foreign speech. The book gives the root one English word (wave I-5 ruling 7; overlay `lag-stammering-isaiah`), so the draft's "strange" is replaced. *ʿimqê śāp̄āh miššᵉmôaʿ*, literally "deep of lip beyond hearing", is "of speech too deep to comprehend" (ASV "of a deep speech that thou canst not comprehend").

*ʿam nôʿāz* "the fierce people". *nôʿāz* occurs only here. ASV and JPS 1917 "fierce" connect it with *ʿzz* "be strong, be insolent" (recalled). NJPS "the barbarian folk" agrees with a proposed reading *lōʿēz* "speaking a foreign tongue" (cf. Ps 114:1; recalled, not verified). The line keeps ASV's reading of MT (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`).

paragraphs.text: חֲזֵ֣ה צִיּ֔וֹן קִרְיַ֖ת מֽוֹעֲדֵ֑נוּ עֵינֶיךָ֩ תִרְאֶ֨ינָה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם נָוֶ֣ה שַׁאֲנָ֗ן אֹ֤הֶל בַּל־יִצְעָן֙ בַּל־יִסַּ֤ע יְתֵֽדֹתָיו֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וְכָל־חֲבָלָ֖יו בַּל־יִנָּתֵֽקוּ׃

i18n.en: Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts! Your eyes shall see Jerusalem, a quiet habitation, a tent that shall not be moved, whose stakes shall never be pulled up, and none of whose cords shall be broken.
i18n.he: חֲזֵ֣ה צִיּ֔וֹן קִרְיַ֖ת מֽוֹעֲדֵ֑נוּ עֵינֶיךָ֩ תִרְאֶ֨ינָה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם נָוֶ֣ה שַׁאֲנָ֗ן אֹ֤הֶל בַּל־יִצְעָן֙ בַּל־יִסַּ֤ע יְתֵֽדֹתָיו֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וְכָל־חֲבָלָ֖יו בַּל־יִנָּתֵֽקוּ׃

notes.official:
*qiryaṯ môʿăḏēnû* "the city of our appointed feasts". *môʿēḏ* is an appointed time or feast, and the book renders the plural "appointed feasts" at 1:14. ASV has "the city of our solemnities", JPS 1917 "the city of our solemn gatherings", NJPS "our city of assembly".

*nāweh šaʾănān* "a quiet habitation" (ASV). *šaʾănān* means "at ease, untroubled" (32:9, 11), and the book prints "quiet" for the same root at 32:18. JPS 1917's "a peaceful habitation" is the book's wording for *nᵉwēh šālôm* at 32:18, so "quiet" keeps the two phrases distinct. *ʾōhel bal-yiṣʿān* "a tent that shall not be moved": *ṣʿn* occurs only here and means "pack up, move (a tent)" (BDB; recalled). The tent's *yᵉṯēḏōṯ* are "stakes" (overlay `yated-peg-stake-isaiah`, tent context), and its *ḥăḇālîm* are "cords"; the same cords come back, slack, in v. 23 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י אִם־שָׁ֞ם אַדִּ֤יר יְהוָה֙ לָ֔נוּ מְקוֹם־נְהָרִ֥ים יְאֹרִ֖ים רַחֲבֵ֣י יָדָ֑יִם בַּל־תֵּ֤לֶךְ בּוֹ֙ אֳנִי־שַׁ֔יִט וְצִ֥י אַדִּ֖יר לֹ֥א יַעַבְרֶֽנּוּ׃

i18n.en: But there YHWH will be mighty for us, a place of broad rivers and streams, where no galley with oars shall go, and no mighty ship shall pass.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י אִם־שָׁ֞ם אַדִּ֤יר יְהוָה֙ לָ֔נוּ מְקוֹם־נְהָרִ֥ים יְאֹרִ֖ים רַחֲבֵ֣י יָדָ֑יִם בַּל־תֵּ֤לֶךְ בּוֹ֙ אֳנִי־שַׁ֔יִט וְצִ֥י אַדִּ֖יר לֹ֥א יַעַבְרֶֽנּוּ׃

notes.official:
*ʾaddîr* occurs twice, in *ʾaddîr YHWH lānû* and *ṣî ʾaddîr*. ASV and JPS 1917 render it "in majesty" in the first clause and "gallant" in the second; NJPS has "in His greatness" and "mighty craft" (all checked). This book reserves "majesty" for *gāʾôn* (overlays `gaon-pride-human-arrogance-isaiah`, `hadar-splendor-isaiah`) and already renders *ʾaddîr* "a mighty one" at 10:34. The line therefore gives the word one rendering in both places: "YHWH will be mighty for us … no mighty ship" (overlay `addir-mighty-isaiah`). *lānû* is "for us" (ASV "with us").

The first half is compressed: YHWH will be "for us a place of rivers", that is, YHWH himself will be to Jerusalem what broad waters are to other cities, a defence no warship can cross. NJPS states this in a note (checked). *rᵉḥăḇê yāḏāyim* "broad on both sides" qualifies both nouns, as in ASV's "broad rivers and streams". *yᵉʾōrîm* beside *nᵉhārîm* is "streams" under the Isaiah clause of central `yeor-nile-egyptian-loanword` (cf. 19:6). *ʾŏnî-šayiṭ* is "a galley with oars" (ASV).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שֹׁפְטֵ֔נוּ יְהוָ֖ה מְחֹקְקֵ֑נוּ יְהוָ֥ה מַלְכֵּ֖נוּ ה֥וּא יוֹשִׁיעֵֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: For YHWH is our judge, YHWH is our lawgiver, YHWH is our king; he will save us.
i18n.he: כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שֹׁפְטֵ֔נוּ יְהוָ֖ה מְחֹקְקֵ֑נוּ יְהוָ֥ה מַלְכֵּ֖נוּ ה֥וּא יוֹשִׁיעֵֽנוּ׃

notes.official: *šōp̄ṭēnû … mᵉḥōqᵉqēnû … malkēnû* "our judge … our lawgiver … our king" (ASV, JPS 1917). *mᵉḥōqēq* is the participle of *ḥqq* "inscribe, decree", the one who decrees (BDB; recalled); at Gen 49:10 and Judg 5:14 it is a ruler's staff or a commander. NJPS reads the three nouns as titles of rule ("our ruler … our prince … our king"). The line keeps ASV's "lawgiver", a lexical sense of the participle, and the three titles stand in parallel with "he will save us" (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`).

paragraphs.text: נִטְּשׁ֖וּ חֲבָלָ֑יִךְ בַּל־יְחַזְּק֤וּ כֵן־תָּרְנָם֙ בַּל־פָּ֣רְשׂוּ נֵ֔ס אָ֣ז חֻלַּ֤ק עַֽד־שָׁלָל֙ מַרְבֶּ֔ה פִּסְחִ֖ים בָּ֥זְזוּ בַֽז׃

i18n.en: Your cords hang loose; they could not hold firm the base of their mast, they could not spread the sail. Then the prey of a great spoil was divided; the lame took the plunder.
i18n.he: נִטְּשׁ֖וּ חֲבָלָ֑יִךְ בַּל־יְחַזְּק֤וּ כֵן־תָּרְנָם֙ בַּל־פָּ֣רְשׂוּ נֵ֔ס אָ֣ז חֻלַּ֤ק עַֽד־שָׁלָל֙ מַרְבֶּ֔ה פִּסְחִ֖ים בָּ֥זְזוּ בַֽז׃

notes.official:
*niṭṭᵉšû ḥăḇālāyiḵ* "Your cords hang loose". *ḥeḇel* is the noun of the tent "cords" of v. 20, here a ship's rigging (ASV and JPS 1917 "tacklings", NJPS "ropes"). The line uses "cords" in both verses so that the contrast stays visible: Zion's cords will not snap, while the cords of the ship addressed here hang slack (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`). The feminine singular "your" has no named referent. NJPS moves the first half of the verse to follow v. 21 and renders "Their ropes", noting "Heb. 'your'" (checked). *kēn-tornām* is "the base of their mast", and *nēs* is here a sail (overlay `nes-signal-isaiah`, which makes this verse its exception).

*ʾāz ḥullaq ʿaḏ-šālāl marbeh* "Then the prey of a great spoil was divided" (ASV). *ʿaḏ* "prey" is rare (Gen 49:27; recalled). NJPS marks the clause uncertain and reports that an emendation yields "even a blind man shall divide much spoil" (checked). MT is kept (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *pissᵉḥîm bāzᵉzû baz* "the lame took the plunder": the cognate object *baz* is "plunder", as at 10:6 ("to take spoil and to seize plunder"), so the book's distinction between *šālāl* "spoil" and *baz* "plunder" holds. ASV has "prey" for both *ʿaḏ* and *baz*.

paragraphs.text: וּבַל־יֹאמַ֥ר שָׁכֵ֖ן חָלִ֑יתִי הָעָ֛ם הַיֹּשֵׁ֥ב בָּ֖הּ נְשֻׂ֥א עָוֺֽן׃

i18n.en: And no inhabitant shall say, “I am sick”; the people who dwell in it shall be forgiven their iniquity.
i18n.he: וּבַל־יֹאמַ֥ר שָׁכֵ֖ן חָלִ֑יתִי הָעָ֛ם הַיֹּשֵׁ֥ב בָּ֖הּ נְשֻׂ֥א עָוֺֽן׃

notes.official: *hāʿām hayyōšēḇ bāh nᵉśuʾ ʿāwōn* "the people who dwell in it shall be forgiven their iniquity" (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS "folk whose sin has been forgiven"). *nᵉśuʾ* is the passive participle of *nśʾ* "lift, bear" in construct with *ʿāwōn* "iniquity": "lifted of iniquity", that is, forgiven (cf. Ps 32:1 *nᵉśûy-pešaʿ*; recalled). This is the forgiveness sense of the *nśʾ* + sin-noun formula (central `sa-na-pesha-nasa-avon-forgiveness-formula-cross-corpus`, `avon-iniquity-cross-corpus-keyword`). The verse sets the end of sickness ("I am sick") beside the removal of iniquity. *šāḵēn* "inhabitant" is a noun of the root *škn*; it is not the verb of vv. 5 and 16, and the central dwell entry is not applied to it.
